current_activity: establishing Montgomery's tactical HQ at Creullet
notes: Montgomery's tactical HQ (21st Army Group; controlled First US and British Second Armies) set up at Chateau de Creullet on 8 June (europeremembers; Ouest-France; FranceArchives). Two other sources date the arrival 7 June (conflict G005). Visited by Churchill 12 June, de Gaulle 14 June, Eisenhower 15 June, King George VI 16 June.

current_activity: Montgomery meets his army commanders and orders Second Army to regroup and attack with six divisions from Caumont
notes: Event date: 27 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 386). Event definition: General Montgomery meets his army commanders on 27 July and issues new instructions: the First US Army has delivered the main blow, further large-scale British effort on the Orne front is 'definitely unlikely to succeed', and Second Army is to regroup and launch a new attack with not less than six divisions from the Caumont area (p. 386). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 386: "On July the 27th General Montgomery had met his army com- manders and after reviewing the position had issued new instructions"; "Second Army was therefore to regroup and to launch a new attack with not less than six divisions from the area of Caumont". Location: Blay, Calvados (existing place PL0041), where the tactical headquarters stood in late June with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the last documented tactical headquarters place; it is not stated for 27 July. Location support: Ellis does not place the headquarters on 27 July; the nearest earlier row of the unit is the tactical headquarters at Blay (22-23 June). Commander: General Montgomery (Ellis, vol. I, p. 386).

current_activity: Montgomery is promoted Field-Marshal; General Eisenhower assumes direct command of the Allied armies in Northern France
notes: Event date: 1 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 476, 477). Event definition: On 1 September General Montgomery is promoted Field-Marshal and General Eisenhower assumes direct command of the Allied armies in Northern France; from that day General Montgomery no longer coordinates the American army group, which the dataset records in CR0116 (ending 31 August) (p. 476). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 476-477: "General Montgomery was promoted Field- Marshal and General Eisenhower assumed direct command of the Allied armies in Northern France". Location: Blay, Calvados (existing place PL0041), where the tactical headquarters stood in late June with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the last documented tactical headquarters place; it is not stated for 1 September and the headquarters had moved on by then. Location support: Ellis does not place the headquarters; the nearest earlier row of the unit is Blay, which is a long way behind the front by September. Commander: General Montgomery (Ellis, vol. I, p. 386).
